work.title: MasterChef Junior
work.note: MasterChef Junior é um programa de culinária com crianças cozinhando. A referência é o programa de culinária infantil: first, then, next.

pages.question: Como a história dessa obra ajuda você a imaginar a situação de hoje? Diga uma ideia em inglês.

facts.label: Situação
facts.sub: Many American fast restaurants let you build your own meal along a counter: you point, choose and the worker adds each layer. Learn the steps, in order, so you never freeze.

pages.title: How to build your bowl · 1/3
paragraphs: Today, my friend Hector and I go to a bowl restaurant in **Phoenix**. The sun is hot, but the restaurant is cool. A man called Kai says, “Hi! **What kind of bowl?**”

**First**, choose a protein. I say, “**A chicken bowl, please.**” **Then**, Kai asks, “**White rice or brown rice?**” “Brown rice, with beans,” I say. **Next**, he asks about toppings. “**Salsa? Cheese? Guacamole?**” I say, “**Salsa and cheese. No guacamole.**”
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: How to build your bowl · 2/3
paragraphs: **Finally**, Kai asks, “**Anything else?**” “No, **that’s it**. How much?” “Nine dollars,” he says. I pay, and he says, “**Enjoy your bowl!**” It looks so good. Hector says, “**That looks sick!**” and his bowl is full of everything.

I love cooking shows. My favorite is “MasterChef Junior”, a show from 2013, where kids from eight to thirteen cook in a big kitchen. They use pots, pans and a stove. The judges say, “First, then, next, finally.” A bowl is a bit like a recipe too.

pages.title: How to build your bowl · 3/3
paragraphs: At home, you can build a bowl in four steps: first, rice; then, beans; next, toppings; finally, sauce. **Load it up**, and **dig in**!
